test_title: PYST 23: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 08 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A cyclist performing uniform circular motion throws an apple in his direction, the apple moves in a ____________.

options.text: straight line path opposite to the cyclist
circular path opposite to the cyclist
tangential path to the circular path at that point

solution:
The correct answer is __**tangential path to the circular path at that point**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uniform Circular Motion:** When a cyclist is in uniform circular motion, they are moving along a circular path with a constant speed. The velocity of the cyclist is always tangential to the circular path at every point, and the centripetal force acts towards the center of the circle to maintain the circular motion.
 
• **Projectile Thrown by the Cyclist:** When the cyclist throws an apple in their direction, the apple initially possesses two components of velocity:
 
 
• A tangential velocity component due to the cyclist's motion along the circular path at that instant.
 
• An additional velocity imparted by the action of throwing the apple.
 
 
 
• **Resultant Path of the Apple:** According to Newton's first law of motion (the law of inertia), the apple will continue to move in the direction of the tangential velocity component at the point of release. Therefore, the apple follows a **tangential path to the circular motion of the cyclist at that point**.
 
• **Why Not a Circular Path?** The apple does not follow a circular path because, after being thrown, it is no longer under the influence of the centripetal force that keeps the cyclist in circular motion. Instead, it moves freely under the influence of its inertia and external forces such as gravity.
 
• **Correct Answer:** Hence, the correct explanation for the motion of the apple is that it follows a **tangential path to the circular path at that point**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion (Law of Inertia):** An object will continue in its state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force. In this scenario, after the apple is released, it is no longer influenced by the centripetal force, and thus it moves in the direction of its initial velocity.
 
• **Tangential Velocity:** The velocity of an object in circular motion is always directed tangentially to the circular path. At the point of release, the apple carries this tangential velocity, leading to its motion along a straight tangential path.
 
• **Circular Motion Dynamics:** Circular motion is maintained by a centripetal force that acts towards the center of the circle. This force is essential for keeping an object in a circular trajectory. Once the apple is released, it is no longer subject to this force, and hence it does not follow a circular path.
 
• **Gravity's Role:** If we consider gravity, the apple will eventually follow a parabolic trajectory due to the combined effect of its horizontal tangential velocity and the downward gravitational force. However, the initial direction of motion remains tangential.
 
• **Applications:** Understanding the tangential motion of an object in circular motion is crucial in various fields, such as satellite launching, amusement park rides (e.g., roller coasters), and vehicle dynamics while turning on curved roads.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option Analysis:**

 
 
• **Option 1:** "Straight line path opposite to the cyclist" is incorrect because the apple is not influenced by a force to reverse its motion.
 
• **Option 2:** "Circular path opposite to the cyclist" is incorrect as the apple is no longer under the influence of centripetal force.
 
• **Option 3:** "Tangential path to the circular path at that point" is correct as explained above.
 
• **Option 4:** "Circular path as the cyclist" is incorrect because the apple does not stay in circular motion after being released.
 
 
 
• **Real-life Examples:**
 
 
• When a stone tied to a string is whirled in a circle and the string breaks, the stone moves tangentially to the circle.
 
• Water droplets flung off a spinning wheel follow a tangential path.
